title: The Bat-Arsenal
statement_markdown_lines: The Mindflayer has ripped open a portal above Gotham, unleashing a horde of exactly $P$ shadow monsters into the streets.

Batman is perched on a gargoyle, assessing the threat. He checks his utility belt and finds that he currently has $R$ Batarangs and $B$ Smoke Pellets. To neutralize the horde from the shadows without taking damage, Batman needs to use exactly one projectile (either a Batarang or a Smoke Pellet) for every single shadow monster.

He wants to quickly calculate if his current inventory is sufficient to clear the streets. Write a program to help the Batcomputer determine if Batman has enough total projectiles to defeat all the monsters.
The first line contains a single integer $t$ ($1 \le t \le 100$) --- the number of test cases.
Each of the next $t$ lines contains three space-separated integers $R$, $B$, and $P$:
- $B$ ($0 \le B \le 1000$) --- the number of Smoke Pellets.
- $P$ ($1 \le P \le 2000$) --- the number of shadow monsters.
For each test case, output a single line containing `YES` if Batman has enough projectiles for all the monsters, and `NO` otherwise.
You can output the answer in any case (for example, the strings `yEs`, `yes`, `Yes`, and `YES` will be recognized as a positive answer).
In the first test case, Batman has $10$ Batarangs and $5$ Smoke Pellets ($15$ total). There are $12$ monsters. Since $15 \ge 12$, the answer is `YES`.
In the second test case, Batman has $0$ projectiles and $5$ monsters, so the answer is `NO`.
In the third test case, Batman has $200$ projectiles for $200$ monsters, which is exactly enough, so the answer is `YES`.
